claims.text: Google Cloud says private-offer custom discounts and an active Flexible Savings Plan discount do not stack; usage receives the lowest available effective rate. This is a marketplace rule to check when evaluating an Atlas offer, not evidence of a particular Atlas discount. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

AWS says sellers cannot use a private offer to impose service limits: buyers can consume at negotiated prices unless the product itself has a limit. A negotiated Atlas offer should therefore not be assumed to provide a hard spending cap. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-24)

Private offers negotiate commercial terms rather than establish one universal Atlas discount: AWS supports custom pricing and EULAs, while Google Cloud specifies custom pricing, payment schedule, duration and EULA. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

Atlas marketplace subscriptions route invoicing through the marketplace. Atlas still provides a cloud usage summary in credits; MongoDB says marketplace subscribers receive the marketplace invoice instead of its separate tax invoice. AWS likewise says accepted private offers use its normal Marketplace invoicing tools. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)

MongoDB distinguishes privately negotiated AWS Marketplace offers from its public no-upfront-commitment pay-as-you-go listing. The Atlas AWS self-serve procedures explicitly cover Marketplace Subscriptions, not Marketplace Contracts; do not apply those procedures to a private contract without checking its terms. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)

MongoDB’s Azure private-offer listing is separate from pay-as-you-go. It advertises a one-year subscription and usage-based credit consumption covering cluster type, network transfer, backup and support; this listing does not establish every negotiated offer’s term. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-24)

AWS private offers are visible only to the targeted AWS accounts. The buyer must sign in to an account receiving the offer, and accepted offer details are available under Manage Subscriptions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-24)

On Microsoft Marketplace, accepting a private offer agrees to its terms but does not complete the purchase. The buyer must also purchase or subscribe; standard SaaS flows additionally require vendor account configuration and confirmation, with a documented exception for Azure Native ISV offerings. (high confidence) (verified as of 2025-12-15)

Google Cloud private offers specify a Cloud Billing account and either upfront prepay or monthly postpay scheduling. After the term ends, continued use at list price is available only for some pricing models; renewal or a replacement offer should be arranged with the vendor. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

Seeing an Azure offer does not establish purchase eligibility. An Atlas-related Q&A cautions against that assumption, while Microsoft’s troubleshooting guidance requires the correct billing account, roles and purchase-policy settings. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-12-15)

One Reddit participant reports paying for MongoDB Atlas through AWS Marketplace made internal finance approval easier. This is anecdotal evidence for procurement convenience; the comment does not identify a private offer or quantify savings. (low confidence)

Offer access is tied to the designated cloud billing identity: AWS requires the receiving AWS account, while Google requires access to the Cloud Billing account named in the offer. Check that identity before troubleshooting an invisible offer. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-24)

An AWS private offer must be accepted before its offer expiration date; acceptance turns it into an agreement. The deadline for accepting an offer is distinct from the resulting service agreement's duration. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-24)

Microsoft says Azure consumption-commitment credit applies to purchases that are Azure benefit eligible. A private offer alone does not establish that a particular Atlas purchase qualifies; verify the offer's eligibility and your agreement. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-04-29)
